worked_solution:
Evaluating $F(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
F\,(\frac{\pi }{2})={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t
$$

Then, computing the definite integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{\pi }{2}) & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =-0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
